draft.title: Flashback
card: A flashback interrupts the main story to show an event from earlier. The story jumps back in time, then returns to the present.
Writers signal it in different ways, such as a change in tense, a memory, a dream or a line like "Years before, ...".
A flashback can reveal a character's past, such as why Omar fears water after a childhood accident.
It can also explain the present, by showing the earlier event that caused something happening now.
draft.remember: A flashback pauses the story to show an earlier event, which helps explain a character or the present.

a.q: A story follows Jo walking into a new school. The next paragraph shows Jo at her old school, saying goodbye to her friends. What technique is this?
a.why: The story stops following Jo's first day and shows an earlier event, the goodbye. That is a flashback. Foreshadowing would hint at something still to come, not show the past.
a.clue: Which way in time does the story jump?

b.q: Mara refuses to touch the piano in her aunt's house. The story then shows her at age seven, being scolded after breaking a piano at a recital. What does this flashback do?
opts: Explains why Mara avoids the piano now
Hints that Mara will play the piano later
Introduces a new setting for the whole story
Shows what Mara's aunt will do next
b.why: The scene from Mara's childhood is an earlier event that explains her present behaviour. It does not point ahead to what she will do. It looks back to show the cause.
b.clue: Ask what the earlier scene helps the reader understand about now.

b.best: Explains why Mara avoids the piano now
